item.title: Emotion by Design: The Emotional Architecture of Consumer Behaviour in an Era of Emerging Technologies
item.content:encoded:
Aude Rychalski, ESSCA School of Management

Varsha Jain, ESSCA School of Management

Elodie Jouny-Rivier, ESSCA School of Management

Anupama Ambika, IMT

This Special Issue invites interdisciplinary contributions exploring how emerging technologies like AI, AR, VR, XR, and others dynamically shape consumer emotions, eventually influencing identity and behaviour. The issue welcomes theoretical, empirical, and methodological paper submissions from consumer behaviour, consumer psychology, human technology interaction, digital media, and related areas.

The focus is on exploring the mechanisms, processes, and consequences in the context of technology-enabled emotion engineering. Additionally, discussions are encouraged on consumer autonomy, well-being, and broader implications of emotionally engineered consumer behaviour.

Appel publié par Journal of Consumer Behaviour. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • How emerging technologies (AI, AR, VR, XR, and others) shape consumer emotions
  • Influence of technology-induced emotions on consumer identity and behaviour
  • Mechanisms and processes of technology-enabled emotion engineering
  • Consequences of emotionally engineered consumer behaviour
  • Consumer autonomy in the context of emotional technology design
  • Consumer well-being implications of emotion engineering
  • Broader societal implications of emotionally engineered consumer behaviour

Timeline

  • November 1, 2026: Submissions window opens
  • December 30, 2026: Submissions window closes

item.title: Educational Immersion for All: Accessibility and Inclusion in eXtended Reality
item.content:encoded:
Andrea Antonio Cantone, University of Salerno

Dragan Ahmetovic, University of Milano

Paloma Diaz, Universidad Carlos III de Madrid

Giuliana Vitiello, University of Salerno

This special issue explores how immersive technologies such as Virtual Reality, Augmented Reality, and Mixed Reality can be designed and implemented to create equitable educational experiences that serve all learners. While immersive technologies offer significant potential for engaging students through interactive, embodied learning, many current applications lack adequate accessibility and inclusive design considerations, potentially creating new digital divides.

The special issue welcomes interdisciplinary research integrating perspectives from human-computer interaction, educational technology, accessibility research, and learning sciences. It seeks contributions investigating how immersive technologies can support diverse learners, including students with disabilities, neurodivergent learners, and individuals from varied cultural and socio-economic backgrounds.

Original research articles, empirical studies, case studies, and evidence-based methodological analyses addressing accessibility challenges, design frameworks, adaptive systems, evaluation methods, and inclusive practices in XR educational environments are invited for submission.

Appel publié par Behaviour & Information Technology. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Design and development of accessible and inclusive immersive learning and training environments
  • Inclusive design frameworks and guidelines for immersive educational technologies
  • Immersive technologies supporting students with disabilities (e.g., cognitive, sensory, motor, neurodevelopmental conditions)
  • Adaptive and personalized immersive learning and training experiences
  • Accessibility challenges and solutions in XR educational interfaces
  • Use of immersive technologies to support neurodivergent learners
  • Evaluation methods for accessibility, usability, and user experience in immersive educational systems
  • Immersive technologies for social skills training and behavioral learning
  • AI-driven adaptive systems in immersive learning environments
  • Multimodal and embodied interaction techniques for accessible XR learning
  • Immersive simulations for inclusive education and special education
  • XR technologies for experiential and collaborative learning in inclusive classrooms
  • Ethical, social, and accessibility implications of immersive technologies in education

Timeline

  • November 30, 2026: Manuscript deadline

item.title: Immersive Technologies in Mobile Applications: Transforming Business Landscapes
item.content:encoded:
Immersive technologies—such as Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR), and Mixed Reality (MR)—are reshaping how businesses engage customers, deliver services, and create value. As these technologies mature and become more accessible through mobile applications, organizations across industries—including retail, tourism, entertainment, healthcare, and education—are exploring their service applications and strategic potential. Immersive technologies not only enhance user experience but also enable new business models, operational efficiencies, and competitive differentiation.

Appel publié par Industrial Management & Data Systems. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • User engagement and behaviour in immersive mobile applications
  • Adoption and diffusion of immersive technologies in organizations
  • Design principles for mobile immersive applications
  • Business innovations enabled by immersive technologies across industries
  • Ethical dimensions, accessibility challenges, and long-term societal impacts immersive mobile applications

Timeline

  • February 1, 2026: Opening date for manuscript submissions
  • September 30, 2026: Closing date for manuscript submissions
